paragraphs: My name is Mia, and I am ten years old. Tonight is Star Night at our school. It is a small camp on the school field. The camp is only for our class, and some parents help. Teacher Kim gives us a timetable on Friday morning. I read it to Lily and Leo. Leo wants to know every time. "What do we bring?" he asks.

We come to the field at half past four. We bring a blanket and a small bag. At five o'clock, we have dinner together. We eat rice and chicken from the school kitchen. The grass is soft and warm. At a quarter to six, we put our blankets on the grass. The sun goes down at about six o'clock. It is not dark yet. Pip stays at home.

At half past six, we have a science talk. Teacher Kim tells us about stars. A star is a very big ball of fire that is far away. At a quarter past seven, we have a star quiz. It is a friendly competition, and every team gets a sticker. My team is Lily, Leo, and me. Leo knows many answers, but he talks too loudly.

At a quarter to eight, we look at the sky. It is dark now, and the stars are bright. "Can we see the moon?" asks Lily. "Perhaps," says Teacher Kim. "The moon comes up late tonight." We wait together on the blankets. Leo points at a bright light. "I see a star!" he says. Teacher Kim smiles and says that it is a plane. At eight o'clock, our parents come, and Star Night finishes. It is a very good night.
